newsitem.title: USA: US Justice urges approval of revised Thomson deal.
newsitem.headline: US Justice urges approval of revised Thomson deal.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Dept said Tuesday it had asked a federal judge to approve a revised settlement involving Thomson Corp's acquisition of West Publishing Co in a deal that brought together two of the nation's largest legal publishers.
It said the revised settlement required the newly formed company to charge lower fees to competing firms that want to provide publications using the widely relied upon West page numbering system.

The Justice Department said the revised consent decree remedies any harms from the acquisition, which initially had been approved in June. Six states joined the Justice Department in supporting the new terms of the settlement.

The Justice Department also said it filed a motion opposing a request by Lexis-Nexis, a competitor of Thomson and a unit of the Anglo-Dutch publishing conglomerate Reed-Elsevier, to intervene in the case.
The Justice Department rejected as "unfounded" concerns by Lexis-Nexis over the acquisition. Lexis-Nexis has objected to the deal.
